schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE INSURANCE (
    PID INT,
    TIV_2015 NUMERIC,
    TIV_2016 NUMERIC,
    LAT NUMERIC,
    LON NUMERIC,
    PRIMARY KEY (PID),
    CHECK (TIV_2015 >= 0),
    CHECK (TIV_2016 >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT ROUND(SUM(TIV_2016),2) TIV_2016 FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015 HAVING COUNT(*)>1) AND (LAT,LON) IN (SELECT LAT,LON FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY LAT,LON HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
q2: SELECT SUM(BASE.TIV_2016) AS TIV_2016 FROM ( SELECT A.PID, A.TIV_2016 FROM (SELECT * FROM INSURANCE WHERE TIV_2015 IN (SELECT TIV_2015 FROM (SELECT TIV_2015, COUNT(*) AS N FROM INSURANCE GROUP BY TIV_2015)BASE15 WHERE N>1) ) A LEFT JOIN INSURANCE B ON A.PID !=B.PID AND A.LAT=B.LAT AND A.LON=B.LON WHERE B.PID IS NULL )BASE

counterexample: INSERT INTO INSURANCE (PID, TIV_2015, TIV_2016, LAT, LON) VALUES (1, 1000, 1234.567, 0.1, 0.1);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent because Q1 rounds the sum of TIV_2016 to 2 decimal places, while Q2 does not round the sum. This can lead to different results if the sum of TIV_2016 has more than 2 decimal places.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have a sum of TIV_2016 that, when rounded to 2 decimal places, is different from the sum without rounding. This can be achieved by having a sum of TIV_2016 that ends in 0.5 when rounded to 2 decimal places.
